body: Live hidden-console probes (Esc interrupt, Ctrl+B background for Bash and subagent, statusLine stdin dump) were not run: the auto-mode permission classifier denied the first step (writing the probe settings/mcp config for a self-driven hidden claude) as 'Tmux Self Drive'. The probe scripts are left ready to run by the user in scratch/planner/probe/; statusLine fields were taken from the docs plus the shape of a real stdin the user's own statusline.py already saves (~/.claude/statusline_last_input.json, 2.1.281).

Running tool calls come from new async hooks (`cctg hook ToolStatus` on PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure with "async": true), not from the transcript stream: an interactive main transcript writes a tool_use record only when the tool finished (TASK-016), so the stream cannot say what runs now. Measured cost per call (dev build): ~10 ms with a live hub, ~313 ms with the hub down, both off Claude Code's critical path because the hook is async; calls inside subagents are skipped before any POST. Alternative: the transcript stream only (shows a call only after it ended; no Ctrl+B window).

Esc/Ctrl+B are pressed by `cctg agent` itself (a direct child of its claude): FreeConsole + AttachConsole(claude pid) + CreateFileW(CONIN$) + WriteConsoleInputW, one press at a time, announced to the hub as Register.console_keys (Windows only, claude pid known) and driven by hub->agent `console_key` / agent->hub `console_key_done` (no wire VERSION bump). The live probe that proves Esc/Ctrl+B act like the keyboard is still to be run by the user (the auto-mode classifier denied the planner's hidden-console run); if it fails, the agent stops announcing console_keys and the hub shows no buttons. Alternative: a separate helper process or a documented Claude Code command (none exists in the channels or hooks docs; Stop hooks do not fire on interrupt).

The status message is per slot, persisted as Slot.status {message_id, pinned} in registry.json (skipped when empty), created only for a live current session after its separator, pinned once (pinChatMessage, disable_notification), its pinned_message service notice deleted only when it names a status message; edits go through Op::Edit (coalesced) at most once per Options::status_every (5 s in the hub, off by default so existing tests keep their op sequences), except right after a button press. A deleted message is sent and pinned again. Alternative: re-send a fresh message per session (more pins, more metered sends) or edit on every event (edit storms).

`cctg statusline` posts the status-line numbers as a `status_line` hook event through the existing hook endpoint (same secret, same device config, 150 ms budget) and prints the user's own `statusLine.command` from $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude settings, run with the same stdin through Git Bash (CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH, EXEPATH, git.exe on PATH) or PowerShell, guarded against recursion by CCTG_STATUSLINE; without a user command it prints `model · ctx N% · 5h N% · 7d N%`. No client-side throttle: Claude Code already debounces the command (300 ms) and runs it per assistant message; the hub paces edits. Alternative: a new HTTP path or agent-link message (the statusline process has no link) or a state file per session for client throttling.

Stop hooks do not fire on a user interrupt (hooks docs), so the turn ends in the status message by three signals: Stop, an agent ack of a pressed Esc, and Claude Code's own `[Request interrupted by user` note read by the stream (once per transcript byte, so a rewind cannot end a newer turn). Alternative: time out a thinking status after N minutes (wrong for long turns).

The ⏬ (Ctrl+B) button ships in code but off: slots::Options::background_button defaults to false and the hub does not turn it on, because the live probe never got a foreground Bash to inject into (probe.ctrlb_bash, probe.esc_bash). ⏹ (Esc) is on: the probe MCP child injected Esc into its parent claude console and the turn was cancelled with no Stop hook, so the hub ends the turn on the agent's console_key_done ok. Alternative: leave ⏬ out entirely (the Ctrl+B code path and wire variant are small and tested with a flag mutation, M13).

Reference workspace lives in %TEMP%/cctg-t029-rev2 (git archive HEAD + planner patch + fixes), not scratch/reviewer2/ws: a Cargo project under scratch/ gets IDE-indexed and locks the folder (TASK-018 lesson). scratch/reviewer2 keeps task029.patch, hashes, verify/build scripts and test outputs. Alternative rejected: ws under scratch as the spawn prompt suggested.

cctg statusline now exits with the user status line command exit code (Claude Code blanks the line on non-zero), own line keeps exit 0. Alternative rejected: always exit 0 (the planner version), which shows output Claude Code would have hidden.

A turn ended by Esc (agent console_key_done ok, or an interrupt note in the stream) also quiets the session permission prompts like Stop does, so the waiting icon and the status line drop; reproduced stuck at "Ждёт разрешения" with the stop button. Alternative rejected: only Activity::stop (planner).

Kept the disabled background (Ctrl+B) button code instead of cutting it: OPEN_DECISIONS Q1 approved it behind background_button=false, and ConsoleKey::Background already on the wire keeps old console_keys agents from decoding a new key kind later. Alternative: cut ~120 lines now and add a capability when the probe passes.

Built the pristine planner tree and the fixed tree into the same CARGO_TARGET_DIR: the uplifted debug/cctg.exe and lib of the other tree were reused (stale binary, then bogus E0308 on statusline::run). Needed cargo clean -p cctg; one target dir must serve one workspace path at a time.

A written Esc shows "Esc sent" without the stop button until Stop, an interrupt note, the next prompt or SessionEnd; alternative: keep the button for a retry. Rejected because a second Esc after an already stopped thinking-phase turn (no Stop, no note) would land in an idle prompt.

Pin notices are filtered by sender == getMe.id in hub::route_inbound (ServiceMessage.from, never logged); alternative: carry sender_is_bot into the slots actor. The router already owns update classification, so the actor stays unchanged.

cctg statusline exits with the user command exit code (docs: non-zero or empty output blanks the status line); when the command is missing, cannot start or times out, cctg prints its own line and exits 0. Alternative from PLAN_V2: print nothing on start failure. Rejected: our shell detection can differ from Claude Code, an own line is more useful than a silent blank.

statusLine padding/refreshInterval/hideVimModeIndicator are documented in docs/poc.md as fields to copy into the cctg --settings file; alternative: generate merged settings at launch. Rejected: no launcher exists in this task and the user has none of these fields.
PLAN_V2 asks to restore the console Ctrl handler after a press. Rejected: after FreeConsole the agent has no console, so no Ctrl events can reach it; the ignore flag only matters while attached.

PLAN_V2 asks to drop cwd/transcript from the status_line POST. Rejected: every hook POST carries them to the same local hub, the hub ignores them for status_line, and removing them needs a wire special case.

Transient pin failures stay "not tried again until restart" as in the planner patch; a retry cadence was not added (orchestrator scope list does not name it, an unpinned but edited status is the only effect).

Reused the leftover %TEMP%/cctg-t029-rev2-target as the single target dir (deps already built) and deleted it at the end, together with the reference workspace; alternative: a fresh target dir, rejected for build time on a memory-tight host. Leftover dirs cctg-t029-rev2 and cctg-t029-review1 in %TEMP% are not this stage's and were left in place.

Verdict NEEDS_WORK rather than PASS: forged/stale presses and wire compat hold, but turn tracking misses channel-started turns (no UserPromptSubmit evidence) and a terminal-answered prompt hides stop for the rest of the turn; the log claim that an interrupt quiets prompts is not in code. Alternative PASS with known limits rejected: both hit the main Telegram flow.

M2: a prompt stops counting as waiting when a ToolStart/ToolEnd hook of the same session arrives at least PROMPT_SETTLE (2 s) after the prompt came in; the interrupt note quiets like Stop. Alternative from the review (quiet on any ToolEnd or stream Result) rejected: async PostToolUse of the previous call and stream lines (unbounded lag) routinely arrive after the next call's prompt and would show stop while the prompt still waits.

m1: tool_start no longer sets turn (running alone drives the tool phase and busy). Alternative (ignore starts after stop until the next prompt) rejected: after a hub restart mid-turn no prompt comes and running calls would never show.

m4: activity map is pruned to live top-level sessions after every hook instead of by followup.ended_sessions; the merged TASK-039 reaper already fed ended_sessions, the retain also covers the reused-pid end that is not in that list. Alternative: add reaped ids only, rejected as it leaves the reused-pid path.
